title: Batavian Republic
capsule: The Batavian Republic was a French-client state established in the northern Netherlands in January 1795 after French Revolutionary forces and Dutch Patriot exiles ousted stadtholder William V of Orange, who fled to England. Modeled on the French Republic, it adopted a unitary constitution in 1798 after extended factional conflict between federalists and unitarists, formally abolishing the old provincial sovereignty of the Dutch Republic. Napoleon's reorganization of his empire transformed it successively into the Kingdom of Holland (1806) and then into direct annexation to France in 1810, which lasted until Allied liberation in late 1813.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Batavian Republic occupied essentially the territory of the former Dutch Republic and its extent is precisely documented; its from date of 1796 in the dataset reflects partial consolidation a year after initial proclamation.
